messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: 2 alerts triggered for service=encoder-web-canary cluster=prod-us-west at 2026-03-14T22:05:27Z. Suspected regression after today's deploy v2.1.3-canary.
noah: I’m on it. seeing crashloops on 3/3 canary pods in us-west-2, readiness failed rapidly.
sara: logs show readiness probe `/healthz` returning 503 then container restarts with OOMKilled on one pod. short traces below.
sara: ```
2026-03-14T22:04:58Z encoder-web-canary-5b7d: readiness check failed: GET /healthz -> 503
2026-03-14T22:05:01Z encoder-web-canary-5b7d: container terminated with exit code 137 (OOMKilled)
```
ryan: HPA also scaled up then down weirdly, metric agg shows a sudden CPU spike then scale-to-zero attempt from autoscaler. might be misconfigured minReplicas.
miguel: can we confirm this is only canary? any sign of Dedicated or Hosted traffic hitting these pods?
noah: only canary target group. we route 5% traffic to canary but traffic pattern spiked during rollout traffic split. customer impact is limited but some inference requests got 503s.
prod-oncall: paging customers? no, small percentage but need quick mitigation. escalate if rollout affects other regions.
sara: initial hypothesis: new config in `deployment.yaml` changed resource requests/limits and liveness/readiness timeouts shorter. also the new encoder allocs spike memory at cold start.
noah: rolling back would be fastest. deploy-bot: detected rollout in progress: `kubectl apply -f k8s/encoder/v2.1.3-canary.yaml` at 22:01:12Z.
noah: trying `kubectl rollout undo deployment/encoder-web --to-revision=10` on canary subset. I’ll pause the rollout and scale canary to 0.
ryan: before undo, can we flip the feature flag kill-switch to stop traffic to canary? ffctl: `toggle ff.encoder.use_v2 false --env prod`
miguel: doing toggle now. `ffctl` output: success, routing set to baseline. :thumbsup:
sara: traffic to canary stopped. but pods still crashlooping, we should drain them gracefully so they don't cause node pressure.
noah: scaling canary down: `kubectl -n prod scale deployment encoder-web-canary --replicas=0` -> succeeded.
noah: also cordon+drain one of the nodes seeing OOMs to avoid spreading eviction. `kubectl drain ip-10-0-45-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60`
ryan: HPA config looks wrong: minReplicas set to 0 for canary in the manifest, autoscaler tried to scale to 0 while we had short-lived traffic bursts. opening pr to fix minReplicas=1 on canary template.
prod-oncall: handoff note: I will remain on-call until 23:00Z, send any followups here. logging incident in ops-incidents:INC-2026-0423.
sara: post-mortem immediate notes: root cause likely a combination of (a) aggressive readiness/liveness timeouts in new deployment, (b) memory spike from encoder cold start, (c) HPA minReplicas=0 which allowed scale-to-zero during spike.
miguel: mitigation done: feature flag flipped, canary scaled to 0, node draining completed. rolling back manifests for canary and reverting HPA change.
noah: rollback verified: canary pods gone, baseline service unaffected. metrics: 503s dropped to baseline within 90s.
ryan: patch PR created: `fix(canary): set minReplicas=1, increase readiness initialDelaySeconds to 15, bump memory request to 512Mi` -> PR #4271.
prod-oncall: customer impact: small percent of inference requests (~0.8% of requests during 22:04-22:07) returned 5xx. escalation not required but log the affected request ids and owners.
alice: uploading logs and heap snapshots to the incident ticket. linking perf traces and flamegraphs.
noah: next steps: gate canary with warmer-start step, add pre-shift traffic ramp, add a canary HPA policy that forbids scale-to-zero during rollout windows, and add a canary readiness smoke test in CI.
prod-oncall: thanks team. I’ll update the incident ticket with timeline and handoff to SRE triage tomorrow morning. :white_check_mark:
